reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring speech disturbance when unilateral weakness was also present (score 2 only).
Using a later rather than the first BP.
name: ABCD² Score

version.label: ABCD² (Johnston et al. 2007)
version.detail: Five factors, 0–7. Risk groups 0–3, 4–5, 6–7 with 2-day stroke risks of 1.0%, 4.1% and 8.1% in the validation cohorts.

purpose: Estimates short-term stroke risk after transient ischaemic attack.
intendedPopulation: Patients assessed early after a suspected transient ischaemic attack.

calculatorNotice.title: Not a standalone triage tool
calculatorNotice.message: ABCD² performed poorly in a large emergency department validation. Imaging and vascular findings, such as atrial fibrillation or carotid stenosis, are not included.

resultStates.label: Lower risk group
resultStates.summary: Score 0–3: 2-day stroke risk 1.0% in the validation cohorts.
resultStates.detail: Group-level estimate; individual risk depends on findings the score does not include.

resultStates.label: Moderate risk group
resultStates.summary: Score 4–5: 2-day stroke risk 4.1% in the validation cohorts.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with imaging, vascular findings and rhythm assessment.

resultStates.label: Higher risk group
resultStates.summary: Score 6–7: 2-day stroke risk 8.1% in the validation cohorts.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with full clinical, imaging and vascular assessment according to local TIA pathways.

clinicalContext.text: Developed to estimate early stroke risk after TIA from bedside features.

clinicalInsights.text: Findings such as atrial fibrillation, symptomatic carotid stenosis or DWI-positive lesions carry risk not captured by ABCD².
A low score does not exclude high-risk mechanisms.

limitations.text: Performed poorly in a large emergency department validation in both low- and high-risk groups.
Does not include imaging, vascular or cardiac findings.

limitations: Depends on the accuracy of the TIA diagnosis.

confounders.effect: Migraine, seizure or syncope can be misclassified as TIA.
Uses the first recorded BP after the event.
Duration and features rely on history.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether an urgent vascular or cardiac cause is present.
Which investigations or treatments are needed.

guideSections.what: A five-factor score (Age, Blood pressure, Clinical features, Duration, Diabetes) for early stroke risk after TIA.
guideSections.whenToUse: Early assessment of patients with suspected TIA, as one part of a comprehensive evaluation.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score each factor from the history and first blood pressure, then sum (0–7).
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used alongside imaging and vascular assessment, not instead of them.

sources.citation: Johnston SC, Rothwell PM, Nguyen-Huynh MN, et al. Validation and refinement of scores to predict very early stroke risk after transient ischaemic attack. Lancet. 2007;369(9558):283-292.
